sections.heading: Preferences and utility in Intermediate Microeconomics
paragraphs: Preferences and utility is studied here as a specific part of Intermediate Microeconomics. Begin by defining the term precisely and identifying the problem it helps explain or solve. Keep the scope narrow: related ideas may interact with it, but they are not interchangeable.

Economics studies choices under scarcity and how incentives shape allocation. Separate a movement along a curve, caused by a change in a variable already on an axis, from a shift of the entire curve caused by another determinant. State whether a claim is positive (testable) or normative (value-based).

For this topic, distinguish the central principle from its assumptions. Ask: what is given, what must be inferred or calculated, what evidence would support the conclusion, and in what circumstances would the conclusion no longer hold? At this level, connect definitions to method. Show how the concept works in a structured example, compare closely related ideas, and explain why a chosen procedure is appropriate.

sections.heading: Worked application

The new equilibrium generally has a higher price and higher quantity, provided the usual upward-sloping supply and downward-sloping demand assumptions hold.

examples.title: Worked application: Budget constraints and consumer choice
steps: A budget constraint identifies affordable bundles given income and prices: p₁x₁+p₂x₂≤m. An interior optimum in the standard smooth model equates the marginal rate of substitution to the price ratio, subject to the budget constraint and preference assumptions. Corner solutions can arise when preferences or constraints make an interior tangency inappropriate.
Identify the assumption or condition on which the explanation depends.
Apply the same principle to a changed case and state what would change in the result.
Write a conclusion that answers the question directly and notes one relevant limitation.
examples.note: Original Student Plug teaching example; not an official university solution or verified past examination question.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a two-good budget equation p₁x₁+p₂x₂=m, what does m represent?
options: Available income or expenditure budget
Marginal utility only
The quantity of good 1
The price elasticity of good 2
practiceQuestions.explanation: m is the total budget available for the two goods in the model.

steps: In a competitive market model, equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. The model assumes, among other things, price-taking behaviour and sufficient market participation; real markets may depart from these assumptions. A comparative-static result predicts how equilibrium changes after a specified exogenous shift.

Government spending equals exports
